style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: clean isometric cutaway illustration, technical drawing style, axonometric projection off-centre, showing a server room rack row layout. The assembly features modular server chassis, GPU trays, and rigid connector pathways. A dense cluster of blades is linked by thick, smooth conduits, but forces data through a single narrow, restricted cable bridge to a secondary rack. Flat muted palette with cobalt and safety yellow accents. Thin consistent line weight, laid over a plain concrete grey plant floor. Recognisable hardware with racks, modules, trays, and connectors with visible depth. One directional light throwing a long cast shadow, generous empty margin, no unlabelled bare abstract boxes, no text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, signature, messy linework
rationale: The article explains a structural routing and bandwidth bottleneck within a multi-GPU architecture. A technical isometric cutaway perfectly illustrates the architectural divide between the fast local NVLink cluster and the slower cross-node PCIe boundary.
subject: isometric cutaway of server racks highlighting a routing bottleneck
core_thesis: Past the node boundary, tensor parallelism stalls because GPUs spend over 90% of runtime swapping small decode-phase messages instead of computing.
core_conflict: Compute capacity vs. interconnect latency (NVLink vs PCIe bandwidth bottleneck)
